# Pre-Lab Question

From equation 3, 
$$y_{dark}=L\left(\frac{m+\frac{1}{2}}{d}\right), \quad m=0, \pm1, \pm2, \dots$$

The first dark fringe on either side of the central maximum corresponds to $m = 0$ (positive side) and $m = -1$ (negative side), which are equidistant from the centre

$$y_{\text{dark}}(m=0) = L\frac{\tfrac{1}{2}\lambda}{d}, \qquad y_{\text{dark}}(m=-1) = -L\frac{\tfrac{1}{2}\lambda}{d}$$

So the separation between the two symmetric first dark fringes is:

$$\Delta y = 2\,y_{\text{dark}}(m=0) = \frac{L\lambda}{d}$$

Substituting values:
$L = 1\ \text{m}, \lambda = 650\ \text{nm} = 650\times10^{-9}\ \text{m}, d = 0.3\ \text{mm} = 3\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}$,

$$\Delta y = \frac{(1)(650\times10^{-9})}{3\times10^{-4}} = 2.1667\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}$$

$$\boxed{\Delta y \approx 2.17\ \text{mm}}$$
